Cc: NetBridge Solutions <eng@netbridge.io>

Subject: Seaglass - Private Deployment: ops sync & cutover cadence

Hi Aisha / David,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the private deployment. Before we schedule the implementation window I want to run a focused networking & ops preflight so we can lock the cutover cadence and call out any gaps up front. Proposed agenda for the network review call:

- Review VPC peering / transit architecture and route propagation
- Confirm CIDR allocations and public IPs for NAT / egress
- Private endpoint naming and DNS flow (split-horizon considerations)
- Mutual TLS / client certs for control plane and appliance auth
- KMS/HSM expectations and key provisioning windows
- On-prem appliance placement, rack + power + network VLANs
- Cutover plan: lab validation -> pilot -> production cutover dates

Attached: seaglass_preflight_questions.xlsx (simple checklist) — please fill sections A/B and return before the call if possible.

Do you have 60 minutes tomorrow (Tue) 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 14:00-15:00 PT? If neither works, propose two alternatives.

I'll loop in our solutions and implementation leads once you confirm.

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Marcus —

Thanks, we can do Wed 2028-04-16 14:00-15:00 PT. I've attached our current VPC diagram (seaglass_vpc_diagram_v2.pdf).

A few quick notes from our side to save time on the call:
- Our primary region is us-west-2; we have a transit gateway for intra-account routing.
- Internal IP space: 10.10.0.0/16 (core), reserved 10.11.0.0/24 for appliances.
- We use an internal proxy for outbound TLS inspection — this may require a short bypass for Redwood egress during the pilot.
- NetBridge (cc'd) will help with BGP peering if we need a direct route.

I'll get the preflight workbook back to you by EOD tomorrow.

—Aisha

Subject: Re: Seaglass - Private Deployment: ops sync & cutover cadence

Kimberly / Priyom — heads-up: Seaglass confirmed Wed 4/16 14:00 PT for the network review. Aisha attached the VPC diagram and called out the internal proxy + transit gateway.

High-level asks for the review (please add / edit):
- Verify VPC peering vs transit-gateway path for both control-plane and data-plane traffic. We want predictable latency for model pulls and telemetry.
- Confirm BGP vs static routes for the pilot. If NetBridge prefers BGP we need prefix lists and ASN.
- Define the private endpoint FQDNs and split-horizon DNS approach (we're recommending using private hosted zone in their account + conditional forward to Redwood).
- KMS: Seaglass will use AWS KMS; confirm if they want Redwood to hold a wrapped key or to use customer-managed keys (CMK).
- Mutual TLS: control plane -> customer appliance cert rotation cadence and SAN requirements.
- On-prem appliance: they listed 1U rack, 2x10G ports. Need final serials and MACs for MAC allowlisting if required.
- Firewall rules: list of outbound IPs/ports for egress and for health checks.

Proposed cutover cadence to propose on the call:
1) Lab validation (redwood testbed) — 2x 4-hour windows over next 7 days.
2) Pilot (subset of traffic) — 48-hour canary window with elevated telemetry.
3) Full cutover — 1-hour production cutover during agreed maintenance window; rollback plan documented.

If that looks good I'll publish a short runbook and the VPC peering template before the call.

Thanks — Marcus

Hi Aisha / NetBridge team,

Thanks for the call today — good alignment. I've uploaded a short VPC peer template and a one-page runbook: redwood_vpc_peer_template.json and the runbook link (https://drive.redwood.ai/runbooks/seaglass-private-cutover-v1).

Technical items we need from Seaglass before lab validation:
- Exact CIDR / prefix lists for BGP (if using): please confirm primary ASN and the prefixes to advertise.
- MTU on the peering path (we've seen MSS issues when MTU < 1500 across proxies).
- Certificate chain for the proxy / TLS inspection appliance — we need the intermediate CA to validate client cert chains during pilot.
- KMS policy decision: CMK grant window or Redwood-wrapped key? If CMK, please provide key alias and ARN.
- Agreed telemetry endpoints for pilot (IP/port).

Attachment: redwood_vpc_peer_template.json (stub) — please populate the fields labeled <CUSTOMER_INPUT> and return.

Action owners from Redwood:
- Kimberly: VPC peer template + runbook updates (ETA 4/16 EOD)
- Priyom: Lab validation windows and appliance pre-provision (ETA 4/18)
- Marcus: Cutover schedule & customer comms (ETA 4/20)

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Implementation Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: David Cross <david.cross@seaglass.ai>

Date: 2028-04-18T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seaglass - technical notes & preflight checklist

Kimberly / Marcus —

Answers inline and attached the completed preflight workbook. A few notes:
- ASN: 64521, prefixes: 10.11.0.0/24 (appliance), 10.12.0.0/22 (services).
- MTU on our peering path is 1500.
- Proxy: we can permit a bypass for Redwood egress during the pilot; however the proxy will terminate TLS and re-initiate to the internet, so we'll need your guidance on cert pinning.
- KMS: we'll use a CMK (alias "alias/seaglass-redwood") and will create a grant for Redwood for the pilot window.

One snag: our security team flagged that the certificate chain for the outbound proxy includes an internal-intermediate CA that isn't on our public list. NetBridge will share the chain separately. Can we shorten the canary window to 24 hours? We have limited maintenance windows in May but can do a tight pilot if telemetry is good.

Attached: seaglass_preflight_questions_filled.xlsx

Thanks — David
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-04-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seaglass - technical notes & preflight checklist — Confirmed cadence & next steps

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, David.

We can accommodate the proxy behavior and the internal-intermediate CA, but we'll need the chain from NetBridge to validate cert paths prior to lab validation. Shortening the canary window to 24 hours is acceptable as long as we do the following during pilot: high-frequency health checks, token-level telemetry retention for 7 days, and an automated rollback trigger on error-rate thresholds.

Confirmed timeline (subject to DocuSign/order completion):
- 4/21-4/22: Redwood lab validation (two 4-hour windows)
- 4/25: Appliance shipment & on-prem rack verification (Seaglass operations)
- 5/02-5/03: Pilot canary (24 hours) — elevated telemetry & manual hold point at 12 hours
- 5/10: Production cutover window (1 hour) with rollback plan on standby

Outstanding deliverables (owners & due dates):
- NetBridge: full proxy cert chain and MAC addresses (due 4/21)
- Seaglass (Aisha/David): CMK ARN & filled preflight workbook (received)
- Kimberly: finalized runbook and VPC peer template (due 4/20 EOD)
- Priyom: confirm appliance provisioning and serials (due 4/22)
- Marcus: publish final customer comms and DocuSign link for the reserved capacity order (sent)
